summary: An exploration of work not just as labor, but as a ritual of obedience, discipline, and the sacrifice of personal comfort for a collective machine.
idea_to_develop: The tension between the 'Hearth' (family) and the 'Field' (the job). The concept that discipline is the tether that allows the kite of the soul to fly.
opening_story: A man stood at the edge of the marketplace, his hands stained with ink and his eyes fixed on the setting sun, asking, 'What is this yoke I carry that provides bread but steals my time?'
closing_story: He returned to his home in the dark, and though his children were asleep, he touched the doorframe with a hand that had built a city, knowing his distance was its own form of protection.

summary: How the constant flow of information acts as a mirror reflecting our own desires and fears rather than reality.
idea_to_develop: The screen as a barrier to the 'now.' The loss of the 'Great Silence' in exchange for a thousand screaming voices.
opening_story: A traveler arrived with a glass tablet that spoke with the voices of a thousand nations, yet he could not hear the wind in the cedars standing right before him.
closing_story: The prophet took the glass and turned it toward the sun until the light blinded the images, saying, 'Only when the mirror is blank can you see the light.'

summary: The loss of nuance and the rise of absolute certainty in a polarized world.
idea_to_develop: The beauty of agnosticism and the 'middle path.' How certainty is a cage that prevents the soul from expanding.
opening_story: Two men stood on opposite sides of a river, each claiming the water flowed only for his own village, cursing the other for drinking from the same stream.
closing_story: A child walked into the water and became wet from both sides, laughing because the river had no name for either man.

summary: The speed of modern judgment and the lack of space for repentance or context.
idea_to_develop: Wrath sent via 'lightning' (technology) versus the slow, cooling walk of physical distance. The permanence of the digital scar.
opening_story: A woman whispered a grievance into the air, and the air turned into a storm of stones that flew across the world in the blinking of an eye.
closing_story: When the storm cleared, she found she had wounded her own brother, for the lightning she threw had traveled in a circle.

summary: The realization that truth is shared among all people, and no one individual holds the entirety of it.
idea_to_develop: The metaphor of the shattered mirror. The necessity of collaboration to see the full image of the Divine.
opening_story: A merchant boasted he sold 'The Truth' in a small silk bag, but when opened, it was only a single shard of glass.
closing_story: The people brought their shards together on the temple floor, and only then did they see the reflection of the heavens.

summary: The psychological danger of only seeking out information that confirms one's own biases.
idea_to_develop: The comfort of the echo versus the growth found in the 'discordant' song of the stranger.
opening_story: A hermit lived in a cave where every wall repeated his own name, until he believed his name was the only word in the language of God.
closing_story: He stepped out into the forest and heard the owl and the wolf, and wept because he had been deaf to the world's true choir.

summary: The drive to ascend and achieve, and the cost of the climb.
idea_to_develop: Ambition as a 'divine hunger' that can either lead to the stars or leave one starving if they ignore the bread of the present.
opening_story: A young man climbed the highest peak to touch the moon, leaving his sandals and his songs at the base of the mountain.
closing_story: At the top, he found the moon was still far away, but the view of his own valley showed him where his heart truly lived.

summary: Living in the shadows of past decisions and 'the doors not opened.'
idea_to_develop: Regret as a ghost that eats the harvest of today. Learning to honor the past without letting it govern the present.
opening_story: An old woman sat by a well, refusing to drink because she lamented the water she had spilled fifty years prior.
closing_story: The prophet poured a fresh cup and said, 'The spilled water has already fed the flowers; will you now die of thirst while the flowers bloom?'

summary: The relationship between the creator and the tool, and the risk of the tool becoming the master.
idea_to_develop: The tool as an extension of the hand. Warning against the 'lamp' that makes us forget the 'sun.'
opening_story: The blacksmith created a hammer so heavy he could no longer lift it, yet he refused to use any other tool.
closing_story: He put down the hammer and used his bare hands to mold the clay, rediscovering the warmth of the earth.

summary: The voluntary giving up of self for a higher cause or the needs of the community.
idea_to_develop: Sacrifice as a way of 'emptying the vessel.' It is the salt that seasons the meat of life.
opening_story: A mother gave her only cloak to a stranger, standing in the snow with nothing but the warmth of her own blood.
closing_story: In her nakedness, she found the wind was no longer her enemy, for she had become one with the breath of the world.
